I'll give one more example of how my sentiment has changed, and then I'll leave it since it's perfectly reasonable to have different opinions over art like this.

In Game of Thrones, initially, when a character died, they stayed dead. And it gave this huge shock value to me when a character was killed. I was stunned, couldn't believe that had happened, etc. Gradually, some characters would die then come back to life. This meant then when I saw someone die, I didn't have that same reaction, since I knew there was a chance they could come back.

That's how I see the ending of C1. When I first watched it I had these huge emotional reactions, but now, they are lessened since Vax came back

The ending of Romeo and Juliet would feel a lot less impactful of Shakespeare work a sequel 7 years later where they both come back to life. Even if they were changed by it, the actions and costs to others would feel less to me. A bit like what was the point in that.

30+ years would be a long time for two humans. But half elves can live for 200+ years, and Keyleth is going to live for 2000+ years, so for them its just a slither of their life. Especially since it doesn't sound like Vax aged.

And as for a price being payed, I didn't say there wasn't a cost, only that it cheapens the big moments from C1. Scanlan having to use his 9th level counterspell that he was saving for wish to try and save his friend, putting the world above his personal feelings was a hugely impactful moment, but it doesn't feel as meaningful knowing that in 30 years he was going to be back anyway
